'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D4C4DC|40–50%}} | title = [[Governor of Alaska|Governor]] | before_election = [[Bill Walker (American politician)|Bill Walker]] | before_party = Independent (politician) | after_election = [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | map = {{Switcher | [[File:2018 Alaska gubernatorial election results map by borough and census area.svg|350px]] | Borough and census area results | [[File:2018 Alaska gubernatorial election results by State House district.svg|350px]] | State house district results | [[File:2018 Alaska gubernatorial election results map by precinct.svg|350px]] | Precinct results }} }} {{Elections in Alaska sidebar}}The '''2018 Alaska gubernatorial election''' took place on November 6, 2018, to elect the [[Governor of Alaska|governor]] and [[List of lieutenant governors of Alaska|lieutenant governor]] of [[Alaska]]. In the primaries for recognized political parties, candidates for governor and lieutenant governor run separately. The winners of each respective primary for governor and lieutenant governor then become a joint ticket in the general election for their political party. Incumbent Independent Governor [[Bill Walker (American politician)|Bill Walker]] was seeking re-election in what was originally a three-way race between Walker, Republican former Alaska state senator [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]], and Democratic former Alaska U.S. Senator [[Mark Begich]]. Despite Walker dropping out on October 19, 2018, and endorsing Begich, Dunleavy won in what was the only gubernatorial gain by a Republican candidate in 2018. As of 2026, this was the last time the governor's office in Alaska changed partisan control. Walker later unsuccessfully ran for governor of Alaska in [[2022 Alaska gubernatorial election|2022]]. This was the only independent-held governorship up for election in a state that [[Donald Trump]] won in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]. ==Independents== ===Governor=== ====Withdrew==== * [[Bill Walker (American politician)|Bill Walker]] (Independent), incumbent governor{{cite web |date=May 6, 2018 |title=Gov. Walker|first=Nathaniel|last=Hertz|work=[[Anchorage Daily News]]|date=April 4, 2018}} This move was widely thought to benefit incumbent Gov. Bill Walker, to foreclose the possibility of a Democratic nominee splitting the vote with Walker against a Republican nominee. However, with the entry of former senator [[Mark Begich]] into the race, Walker withdrew from the Democratic primary and forged ahead with a fully independent bid for reelection.{{cite web|url=https://www.apnews.com/2d0715c18ed8440fac547420b7975c81|title=Former Sen.
